full_judgment: 6. Mr. Salam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner contends that the petitioner is a co-sharer in the land. According to him after the acquisition of superior interest, the petitioner become a tenant in respect of the disputed lard along with other tenants including Atul Chandra Das. The learned Advocate submits that the property in suit being a tank is impartible in nature and as such the pre-emptor become a co-sharer in joint ownership and possession with ether tenants. Mr. Salary has Prefaced his contention by referring to the decision in the case of, Anwara Begunm Chowdhurani and Shamsul Huda Chowdhury Vs. Nur Jahan Begum and others reported in 27 DLR (Appellate Division) 109. There is no dispute with the proposition that after the notification issued under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the status of an under raiyat was upgraded to that of a tenant. There is also no dispute that with the acquisition of rent-receiving interests by the Government, all the intermediary interests disappeared and a person holding land under the landlord became a tenant holding land directly under the Government. These aspects of law have no direct reference to the question raised by the learned Advocate. The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act did not contemplate the merger of all the existing tenancies into one common tenancy and all the tenants under the different tenancies become co-sharers in such a tenancy. The facts of the instant case clearly indicate that the petitioner was a co-sharer of the Touzi No. 358 recorded in C. S. Khatian No. 1. There is no dispute that Hemanga Mohan Bardhan was a co-sharer in the said Khatian. No. 1. This Bardhan settled some land of the disputed tank in favour of Shambhu Charan Misir. The settlement obtained by Shambhu Charan constituted a tenancy distinct and separate from the holding recorded in C. S. Khatian No. 1. It further appears that Shambhu Charan settled the suit land in favour of Atul Chandra Das by a registered Kabuliyat Exhibit B dated 5. 9. 46 in raiyati right. Thus the raiyati right of Atul Chandra Das constituted a holding which was different from the holding of Shambhu Charan and the holding recorded C. S. Khatian No. 1. On an analysis of these facts, it transpires that the contention of Mr. Salain, leads to an absurd proposition of law. By no stretch of imagination it can be conceived that with the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act coming into force, all these three holdings merged into one holding and all the tenants in respect of these different holdings became co-sharers to one common holding, in other words a co-tenancy emerged. The effect of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is that the intermediary interests ceased to exist and the tenants who were holding as under-tenants became tenants directly under the Government. Mr. Salam, however, could not cite any authority in support of his proposition. He has, however, referred to the case of Brindaban Chandra Chowdhury and another Vs. Musammat Rezia Begum and another 16 DLR 77 to contend that Atul Chandra Das, Shambhu Charan and Bardhan became co-sharers with the petitioner.
